caption.text: You come to me expecting another list of foods to avoid, and we end up talking about what we can add back. Expanding someone's food list is often the start of feeling better. If your list keeps shrinking and you still feel bad, book a free call through the link in bio.

Feeling rough and need something easy? This is the smoothie I recommend when you're bloated, puffy and tired: mango, ginger, a scoop of collagen, coconut water and a handful of greens. Save it. Recipe in the caption.

Your lymphatic system moves immune cells, fluid and waste, and it has no pump, so it depends on how you live. Walking, rebounding, sauna, diaphragmatic breathing, beets and greens, berries, citrus, ginger, hydration, dry brushing and regular bowel movements all help. DM us or comment if you'd like support.

I'm an integrative dietitian. Of course I ask about your bowel movements, want every lab from the last five years, and have seventeen follow-up questions before we get to food. After 13 years, the best clues come from the questions nobody asked. Fellow dietitians, what would you add?

SIBO recurrence isn't always about the bacteria. When symptoms come back we look at motility, bile flow, stomach acid, stress and what was never addressed the first time. If you've treated SIBO twice and it keeps returning, that pattern is the clue.

10 easy, balanced, low-histamine snacks for kids and adults. Because eating low histamine should not mean eating nothing: rice cakes with ghee, fresh pear and pumpkin seeds, carrot sticks with hummus made fresh, and more. Save this one.

7 things I'll never do as an integrative dietitian. After 13 years in practice: hand you a 40-supplement protocol, remove every food at once, ignore your sleep, skip your labs, promise a timeline, treat the test instead of the person, or decide before I've listened.

When was the last time you took a smelly one? We all know a bad one, but a persistent change in smell can point to fat malabsorption, bile flow, dysbiosis or an infection. Not a thing to ignore for months. Ask us.

Your food reactions might not be from the food itself. Certain fruits and vegetables carry natural chemicals, pesticide residue and mold that trigger the same symptoms as a true intolerance. We look at the whole exposure, not just the ingredient list.
Your bottom itches? No, persistent itching isn't normal, and no, it's not always pinworms. Yeast, histamine, bile acids and sugar all show up here. Comment below if you want the checklist.

Histamine isn't only about what you're eating. When I work with someone who has reactions to everything, I look at gut infections, mold exposure, hormones, nutrient status and the enzymes that clear histamine. Food is one lever of five.
If you've tried all of these and you're still bloated and constipated, it may be time to look deeper: motility, bile, thyroid, pelvic floor and the microbiome. Here's what I check next.
